key_insight: In flow matching, different paths can produce the exact same learning objective but very different SGD variance, so choosing the path is an optimization problem, not just a modeling detail.
engineering_relevance: For practical generative modeling, path design can materially speed up training and improve stability without changing the target distribution.
method: Analyze stochastic gradient variance under alternative flow-matching paths that share the same marginals and velocity field.
Derive a tight SGD complexity bound for a linear Gaussian setting and identify an optimal linear path within the valid path family.
Formulate PathOpt_theta to minimize variance under the admissible-path constraint, then give a sample-estimable equivalent for numerical search.
evidence_signal: The theory is backed by experiments on Gaussian data, Gaussian mixture models, and real datasets, showing the variance-reduction effect beyond toy settings.
watch_item: Variance minimization must respect the constraint g_t in G(p_t, v_t^*); ignoring it may reduce variance yet still slow convergence or change the FM problem.
paper_title: Same Flow, Different Paths: Variance Reduction in Flow Matching
